interpretation.rootDepth: Table 22 reports ranges of maximum effective rooting depth, not initial depth or a developmental trajectory. Its footnote says larger values apply where soil layering or other restrictions are absent; smaller values may be used for irrigation scheduling, while larger values may be used for modeling soil-water stress or rainfed conditions.
interpretation.depletionFraction: The listed p values apply at ETc approximately 5 mm/day. Preserve FAO-56 adjustment p = pTable + 0.04 × (5 − ETc), limited to 0.1…0.8. The source also says p may be reduced 5–10% for fine-textured clay or increased 5–10% for coarse-textured sand; no such texture adjustment is inferred by this reference inventory.
limitations: Reference values do not establish a catalog-specific active default, crop root-growth trajectory, root-zone initial state, crop coefficient, or measured prediction accuracy.
All entries remain reference-only; exact/common matches do not imply that an annual crop model is appropriate for perennial crops.
No source-backed dynamic canopy, production parameter, or full crop model is inferred from this root table.

sourceArithmeticFixture.classification: source arithmetic reproduction for FAO-56 method; not full reducer validation, a candidate comparison, reference-model agreement, or crop prediction validation
sourceArithmeticFixture.sourceLocation: FAO-56 Chapter 8, Example 37, including its ten-day output table.
sourceArithmeticFixture.pTreatment: Freeze the Example 37 stated p=0.40 for this example reproduction. Although ETc is 6 mm/day, this source example does not substitute the general Table 22 p adjustment. The separate FAO p-adjustment helper remains covered at ETc=6 by its own arithmetic test.
sourceArithmeticFixture.recurrence: Use unrounded daily root-zone water storage/depletion internally, with no daily rain, irrigation, capillary rise, runoff or drainage; compare rounded displayed outputs only.
